title: A Codex 0.165 child cannot point back at the call that spawned it
foundBy: user report (host), reading a cs-campaign viewer site on 2026-11-07: "Opencode shows where they were forked from... but Claude and Codex dont"

evidence.verified: `make ci` passed with exit 0 at 0b15909. `go test ./internal/normalizer/ -run TestNormalizeCodexSubAgentActivityItemJoinsTheSpawn -count=1`: PASS. The test feeds a `spawn_agent` call and the `SubAgentActivity` item that names its child, and the spawn event carries `childSessionId` t2 and the command `spawn /root/state_checks`. Without the change the spawn carries no child and the item is an unrecognized meta event. The tracer reads the fixture `codex/v0.165/multi-agent-run`, an archived Codex 0.165 member, into 6 trajectories. Its four children each carry a parentEventIndex at the parent's spawn call, at events 18, 21, 24 and 27, and the directory test checks those four stamps. TestNormalizeCodexCollabSpawnNoticeNamesTheChild: PASS, the v1 shape written from the source, with no v1 capture behind it.

details: The codex adapter learns which child a `spawn_agent` call started from the `sub_agent_activity` event Codex 0.146 writes, keyed by the call's id. Codex 0.165 writes no such event. It reports the start and end of a sub-agent as an `item_completed` event whose item is a `SubAgentActivity`. That item carries the spawning call's id as its own id, the child's `agent_thread_id` and its `agent_path`. The spawn call's own output names the task alone. So no spawn event carries a `childSessionId`, and the tree stamps no `parentEventIndex` on the child. The viewer's index draws the child under its parent with no way back to the call. The child still names its parent from its own `session_meta`.

notes.text: Multi-agent v1 on 0.165 writes neither record. Its spawn's notice is a `CollabAgentToolCall` item whose `receiver_thread_ids` are the threads it started, read from the 0.165 source, so the adapter now takes the child from there too. No v1 capture exists yet to confirm the shape; the `wait` notices of this run's v2 capture show the struct.
